title: Thyroid Storm
clinicalScenario: Outline only. Planned scope: Diagnostic scoring, beta-blockade, anti-thyroid drug sequence, steroids, supportive care, precipitants, critical care referral. Candidate sources to verify: American Thyroid Association hyperthyroidism guideline; Burch-Wartofsky point scale.

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult (over 18 years) Emergency Department (ED) recognition and drug treatment of thyroid storm (thyrotoxic crisis), based on the Norfolk and Norwich NHS trust guideline for suspected thyroid emergencies (version 3.2, 2022) and the MSD Manual treatment table. Definitive treatment and long-term care are outside this protocol. The American Thyroid Association guideline could not be opened. No Saudi national guideline was found.
findings: Full protocol rebuilt from the source dossier opened on 2026-10-21; exact source locations are recorded in each investigation and medicine row.
The original outline remains preserved; this additive version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: Normal ranges are typical adult values, not from the cited sources.
Symptoms, signs, precipitants, differentials and pathophysiology are standard clinical content and were not extracted line by line.

The Norfolk and Norwich guideline is past its review date (30 August 2025) and the organisation is described only as "the Trust" in the text; the MSD Manual is a reference text, not a guideline. The two differ substantially (for example propylthiouracil 200 mg three times daily versus a 600 mg load), and the American Thyroid Association 2016 guideline was not opened. Both regimens are shown as separate branches; involve a senior endocrinologist early.
Carbimazole dose for storm, duration of iodine, hydrocortisone and prednisolone duration, and the fluid and glucose regimen were not stated in the opened text.

No Saudi national or Saudi Ministry of Health thyroid storm guideline was found; Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) availability of propylthiouracil and Lugol's iodine was not checked. Propylthiouracil carries a liver injury warning.

Renal, hepatic and age adjustments for the drugs added in this revision are from manufacturer labels (UK Summary of Product Characteristics, US prescribing information and a New Zealand data sheet), not from Saudi Food and Drug Authority labels.

pathophysiology.summary: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening exaggeration of thyrotoxicosis, usually in Graves disease, triggered by infection, surgery, trauma, iodine load or stopping antithyroid drugs.
keyMechanisms: Excess thyroid hormone causes fever, tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, agitation, delirium, vomiting and liver dysfunction.
Heart rate control is the first priority because tachycardia, atrial fibrillation and heart failure cause most deaths.
Iodine is given after the thionamide because earlier iodine can feed hormone synthesis and worsen thyrotoxicosis.

Treatment has five parts: control heart rate (beta-blocker), block hormone synthesis (thionamide), block hormone release (iodine, given after the thionamide), reduce conversion and treat adrenal stress (steroid), and support (fluids, cooling, treat the precipitant).

symptoms: Palpitations, sweating, heat intolerance, tremor, agitation, vomiting, diarrhoea, weight loss.
physicalSigns: Fever above 38°C, tachycardia above 110 beats per minute (with or without atrial fibrillation), heart failure, agitation or delirium, goitre or eye signs.
redFlags: Heart failure, atrial fibrillation or delirium.
Burch–Wartofsky score above 45, or 25–45 (impending storm, treat as storm).
precipitants: Infection, surgery, trauma, iodine or contrast load, stopping antithyroid medicines, labour, amiodarone.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Source of infection; normal thyroid function tests

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Low TSH with high T4 and T3
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Confirm; do not wait for results to treat

clinicalManagement.title: Immediate
actions: Recognise by the cardinal features and the Burch–Wartofsky score and start treatment without waiting for blood tests.
Give a thionamide (propylthiouracil) and start iodine only 60 minutes after the first thionamide dose.

clinicalManagement.title: Ongoing
actions: Give steroid (hydrocortisone), then iodine at 60 minutes, then cholestyramine.
Support: IV fluids and glucose, cooling, treat the precipitant and consider central venous monitoring to guide fluids.

clinicalManagement.title: Escalation
actions: Call endocrinology and the high dependency unit; sedation with chlorpromazine 50–100 mg IM if needed.
Avoid beta-blockers in asthma: use a calcium channel blocker if beta-blockade is contraindicated.

clinicalManagement.title: Disposition
actions: Admit to high dependency or intensive care.

regimens.indication: Control heart rate and adrenergic symptoms
regimens.patientGroup: Adults able to take oral medicines
regimens.dose: 80 mg (Norfolk and Norwich); MSD Manual 60–80 mg
regimens.frequency: Three times daily (Norfolk and Norwich); every 4–6 hours (MSD Manual)
regimens.duration: Not faster than 1 mg per minute; a second dose may follow after 2 minutes, then no further dose within 4 hours; stop when the desired heart rate is reached
adjustments: Hepatic insufficiency: consider a lower IV dose
contraindications: not contraindicated in acute severe thyrotoxic heart failure

regimens.indication: Reduce T4 to T3 conversion and cover adrenal stress

renal insufficiency: use with caution
elderly: no dose change, close supervision

guidelineComparison.title: Guideline comparison
columns: Norfolk and Norwich trust guideline v3.2

values: 2 mg over 10 minutes if very unstable
600 mg load then 200–400 mg every 6–8 hours
Lugol's 5 drops four times daily, 60 minutes after the first propylthiouracil dose
Saturated potassium iodide 5 drops every 6 hours; Lugol's 4–8 drops every 6–8 hours; sodium iodide 1 g IV over 24 hours
Hydrocortisone 200 mg IV then prednisolone 20 mg three times daily
Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV every 8 hours or dexamethasone 2 mg IV every 6 hours

learningObjectives: Recognise thyroid storm with the score and give drugs in the right order.
keyPoints: Give iodine only 60 minutes after the first thionamide dose.
Propranolol is not contraindicated in thyrotoxic heart failure; avoid in asthma.

patientEducation: Take antithyroid medicines as prescribed and report fever, sore throat or jaundice.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid iodine-rich supplements and report new symptoms early.
mdtReferrals: Endocrinology and high dependency or critical care.
dischargeCriteria: Not for ED discharge; transfer to high dependency or ward under endocrinology once stable.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Endocrinology follow-up and definitive therapy (iodine-131 or surgery) after the crisis is controlled.
